variants.title: Run the control loop
variants.context: An autonomous system repeats one loop: observe the environment with timestamps and health signals, infer a belief state with uncertainty, select a bounded action that passes the constraints, then act, measure the response, and start again from fresh evidence.
variants.prompt: A warehouse robot is moving down an aisle under normal conditions. Put one cycle of the loop in order.

items.text: Generate feasible trajectories, reject candidates that violate constraints, and expose the chosen plan's assumptions.
Collect timestamped measurements and health signals from the cameras, lidar, encoders, and map.
Track the bounded command, compare expected with measured response, and reobserve before the next cycle.
Fuse current and prior evidence into pose, motion, free space, and the uncertainty around each.

variants.hint: Which step is allowed to produce certainty, and which one only produces evidence?
variants.explanation: Each cycle starts from fresh synchronized evidence, because the action taken changes the environment that produces the next observation.

variants.title: Run the control loop
variants.context: An autonomous system repeats one loop: observe the environment with timestamps and health signals, infer a belief state with uncertainty, select a bounded action that passes the constraints, then act, measure the response, and start again from fresh evidence.
variants.prompt: A person steps out from behind a stack of pallets. Put the cycle that responds to that event in order.

items.text: The planner drops the candidates whose clearance depends on that poorly observed velocity and slows the reference.
The controller tracks the reduced command and the next frame measures whether the gap actually opened.
The tracker associates the cluster with a new track and carries wide uncertainty on its velocity.
The lidar returns a new cluster with its timestamp and the sensor health flags for that frame.

variants.hint: Weak evidence should shrink the action, not the caution.
variants.explanation: Uncertainty travels forward into planning, so a poorly observed track narrows the set of allowed commands.

variants.title: Run the control loop
variants.context: An autonomous system repeats one loop: observe the environment with timestamps and health signals, infer a belief state with uncertainty, select a bounded action that passes the constraints, then act, measure the response, and start again from fresh evidence.
variants.prompt: A camera frame arrives 900 milliseconds late while the platform is still moving. Put the cycle in order.

items.text: Planning rejects the candidates that were only feasible under the fresher estimate and selects a slower plan.
The controller executes the smaller command and the next synchronized observation confirms the new state.
State estimation refuses to treat the stale frame as current and widens the uncertainty on the affected fields.
The time base records the frame age alongside the measurement and marks the sensor as degraded.

variants.hint: A correct but old value is not the same as a current one.
variants.explanation: Freshness is part of the state contract, so an old measurement widens uncertainty instead of passing through as truth.

variants.title: Run the incident loop
variants.context: The incident loop runs in a fixed order: contain unsafe authority, preserve synchronized traces and versions, localize the first invalid assumption, repair the narrowest responsible contract, then requalify before capability is restored.
variants.prompt: A delivery robot clipped a shelf leg and stopped. Put the incident response in order.

items.text: Freeze synchronized traces, software and model versions, maps, calibration, and operator actions.
Change the narrowest responsible contract, dataset, monitor, or operating domain boundary.
Revoke unsafe authority and bring the affected units toward the defined safe state.
Replay the incident class, neighboring scenarios, and transfer timing before restoring capability.
Determine whether the first invalid assumption was in sensing, estimation, planning, monitoring, or control.

variants.hint: What has to happen before anyone starts reading logs?
variants.explanation: Containment comes first and requalification comes last, so no unit keeps authority while the cause is still unknown.

variants.title: Run the incident loop
variants.context: The incident loop runs in a fixed order: contain unsafe authority, preserve synchronized traces and versions, localize the first invalid assumption, repair the narrowest responsible contract, then requalify before capability is restored.
variants.prompt: Three units in a fleet reported the same late fallback transition this morning. Put the response in order.

items.text: Repair only the contract that failed rather than retuning the whole perception stack.
Rerun the affected scenario family and the transfer timing suite before widening capability again.
Restrict the fleet's route and speed capability so no further unit can enter the same condition.
Capture the traces, configuration bundle, and calibration files from all three units before any redeploy.
Compare the three timelines to find the earliest shared assumption that stopped holding.

variants.hint: Fleet containment should not wait for a retrain.
variants.explanation: Capability reduction, route restriction, and quarantine are available immediately, so containment never depends on a model fix.

variants.title: Run the incident loop
variants.context: The incident loop runs in a fixed order: contain unsafe authority, preserve synchronized traces and versions, localize the first invalid assumption, repair the narrowest responsible contract, then requalify before capability is restored.
variants.prompt: An inspection drone landed hard after a localization jump. Put the response in order.

items.text: Fix the responsible contract and tighten the monitor that failed to flag the jump.
Ground the affected airframes and hold them in the defined safe state.
Requalify with the incident scenario, its neighbors, and a hardware in the loop timing run.
Preserve the synchronized flight logs, map version, calibration, and the operator's commands.
Trace whether the jump began in the sensor, the fusion step, the map, or the pose estimator.

variants.hint: The first invalid assumption is usually earlier than the visible symptom.
variants.explanation: Localizing before repairing prevents a fix aimed at the actuator when the failure began in the evidence.

variants.title: Budget the stopping distance
variants.context: Required distance is reaction distance plus braking distance plus clearance plus state uncertainty, where reaction distance is speed times end to end delay and idealized braking distance is speed squared divided by twice the deceleration.
variants.prompt: A vehicle travels at 10 meters per second with an end to end delay of 0.4 seconds and a maximum deceleration of 2.5 meters per second squared. Clearance is 2 meters and state uncertainty is 1 meter. What is the required distance?
variants.hint: Four terms go into the budget, not two.
variants.explanation: Reaction is 4 meters, braking is 100 divided by 5 which is 20 meters, and clearance plus uncertainty adds 3 more, for 27 meters.

mistakes.feedback: That is reaction plus braking only; clearance and state uncertainty are part of the budget.
Braking distance divides by twice the deceleration, so 100 divided by 5 rather than by 2.5.

variants.title: Budget the stopping distance
variants.context: Required distance is reaction distance plus braking distance plus clearance plus state uncertainty, where reaction distance is speed times end to end delay and idealized braking distance is speed squared divided by twice the deceleration.
variants.prompt: A shuttle travels at 20 meters per second with an end to end delay of 0.3 seconds and a maximum deceleration of 4 meters per second squared. Clearance is 3 meters, state uncertainty is 2 meters, and the obstacle is detected 68 meters ahead. What is the distance margin?
variants.hint: Build the whole budget before subtracting it from the detection range.
variants.explanation: Required distance is 6 plus 50 plus 3 plus 2, which is 61 meters, leaving a 7 meter margin at 68 meters.

mistakes.feedback: That subtracts reaction and braking only and spends the clearance and uncertainty margins.
That uses braking distance alone and ignores how far the platform travels during the delay.

variants.title: Budget the stopping distance
variants.context: Required distance is reaction distance plus braking distance plus clearance plus state uncertainty, where reaction distance is speed times end to end delay and idealized braking distance is speed squared divided by twice the deceleration.
variants.prompt: A platform runs at 15 meters per second. A new perception stage raises the end to end delay from 0.2 seconds to 0.6 seconds. How much extra distance does the platform cover before any braking begins?
variants.hint: The question asks for the change, not the total.
variants.explanation: Reaction distance is speed times delay, so the extra 0.4 seconds of pipeline delay costs 6 more meters at 15 meters per second.

mistakes.feedback: That is the reaction distance at the new delay, not the increase over the old one.
That is the reaction distance at the old delay, which is what the change is measured against.

variants.title: Keep the fallback independent
variants.context: A fallback is only real if it detects the violation, gains authority, and reaches a safe state before the hazard window closes, without sharing the dependency that failed. A monitor that consults the failed component is not independent.
variants.prompt: The fallback controller reads the same pose estimate as the primary planner, and that estimate is what failed. What should change?
options: Run the fallback on a second copy of the same estimator for redundancy.
Give the fallback its own evidence path so a bad pose cannot disable both.
Raise the fallback's confidence threshold so it triggers earlier on a bad pose.
optionFeedback: Two copies of one estimator fail together on the same bad input.
Shared dependencies produce common cause failure, so the backup needs different inputs.
A threshold change still leaves the fallback reading the value that was wrong.
variants.hint: Ask what both paths would believe if the shared input is wrong.
variants.explanation: A fallback that shares the failed dependency is not a fallback, so its evidence, compute, and power assumptions are kept explicit and separate.

variants.title: Keep the fallback independent
variants.context: A fallback is only real if it detects the violation, gains authority, and reaches a safe state before the hazard window closes, without sharing the dependency that failed. A monitor that consults the failed component is not independent.
variants.prompt: A monitor detects the violation in 700 milliseconds, but the modeled hazard becomes unavoidable 500 milliseconds after the violation. What does that mean?
options: The fallback loses the timing race and does not support the safety claim.
The fallback is adequate because it always reaches the safe state eventually.
The fallback is adequate as long as its false intervention rate stays low.
optionFeedback: Detection, transfer, and safe state completion all have to fit inside the hazard window.
Reaching a safe state after the hazard is unavoidable does not prevent the harm.
A low false intervention rate says nothing about response time.
variants.hint: Compare the response time distribution with the hazard window, not with the average case.
variants.explanation: The fallback must detect, take control, and reach the safe state before the hazard window closes, so timing is its own gate.

variants.title: Keep the fallback independent
variants.context: A fallback is only real if it detects the violation, gains authority, and reaches a safe state before the hazard window closes, without sharing the dependency that failed. A monitor that consults the failed component is not independent.
variants.prompt: A remote assistant can send a waypoint that the onboard stack executes without passing the authority gate. What is wrong?
options: Remote advice adds network latency that the planner did not budget for.
Remote advice makes the operator responsible for a decision the model made.
Remote advice has become an unmodeled control path around the safety boundary.
optionFeedback: Latency matters, but the real defect is the bypassed constraint check.
Assigning blame does not restore the missing constraint check.
Every command reaching the actuator has to pass the same gate, whoever proposed it.
variants.hint: Which commands are allowed to skip the gate?
variants.explanation: Remote assistance stays bounded, because advice that bypasses the onboard gate becomes a control path with no constraint checks and no tested timeout.

variants.title: Assign the loop stage
variants.context: The architecture splits duties: perception and state build the belief, prediction and planning generate scored candidates, the authority gate rejects commands that break constraints, the controller tracks the reference against real response, and runtime assurance revokes authority and selects a fallback.
variants.prompt: Match each stage to the duty it owns.

pairs.label: Perception and state
pairs.detail: Fuse evidence over time into pose, tracks, and free space while carrying uncertainty forward.

pairs.label: Prediction and planning
pairs.detail: Forecast relevant motion and score feasible candidates for progress, risk, and constraint margin.

pairs.label: Authority gate
pairs.detail: Reject stale, uncertain, infeasible, or out of domain commands before they reach the actuator.

pairs.label: Controller and plant
pairs.detail: Track the bounded reference, enforce actuator limits, and expose measured tracking error.

pairs.label: Runtime assurance
pairs.detail: Monitor the whole loop independently, revoke primary authority, and record why the transition happened.

variants.hint: Two stages can say no; they say no to different things.
variants.explanation: Separating the duties is what lets a team name which contract failed instead of blaming one opaque output.

variants.title: Assign the loop stage
variants.context: The architecture splits duties: perception and state build the belief, prediction and planning generate scored candidates, the authority gate rejects commands that break constraints, the controller tracks the reference against real response, and runtime assurance revokes authority and selects a fallback.
variants.prompt: Five symptoms appear in one week of field data. Match each to the stage whose contract it belongs to.

pairs.label: Perception and state
pairs.detail: Two sensors disagree about an obstacle and the fused output averaged them into nothing.

pairs.label: Prediction and planning
pairs.detail: The selected trajectory assumed a pedestrian would keep walking at a constant speed.

pairs.label: Authority gate
pairs.detail: A command computed from a 900 millisecond old frame still reached the actuator.

pairs.label: Controller and plant
pairs.detail: The actuator saturated on a slope and the realized path drifted from the reference.

pairs.label: Runtime assurance
pairs.detail: The primary stack kept steering for two seconds after a compute deadline was missed.

variants.hint: Ask which contract promised to prevent each symptom.
variants.explanation: Disagreement, feasibility, freshness, tracking error, and revocation are separate promises, so each symptom points at one owner.

variants.title: Assign the loop stage
variants.context: The architecture splits duties: perception and state build the belief, prediction and planning generate scored candidates, the authority gate rejects commands that break constraints, the controller tracks the reference against real response, and runtime assurance revokes authority and selects a fallback.
variants.prompt: A review reads five more traces. Match each finding to the stage that owns it.

pairs.label: Perception and state
pairs.detail: A track vanished during a short occlusion and reappeared with invented certainty.

pairs.label: Prediction and planning
pairs.detail: Every candidate route was scored for comfort before geometry limits were applied.

pairs.label: Authority gate
pairs.detail: A commanded speed above the operating domain limit was accepted at a construction zone.

pairs.label: Controller and plant
pairs.detail: Commanded and measured yaw diverged steadily and no fault was raised.

pairs.label: Runtime assurance
pairs.detail: A fallback was selected but no record explains which condition triggered it.

variants.hint: Feasibility is checked before scoring, and freshness is checked before actuation.
variants.explanation: Candidates are filtered for constraints before comfort, and every authority transition leaves a reason in the trace.
